title: Fourteen Springs and One Short Margin
subtitle: 文学创作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学创作（人与社会·文学艺术）
meta: 主题语境：文学创作（人与社会·文学艺术）　|　核心词汇：draft　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 draft 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 my teacher ① wrote a draft that no editor in the office would have accepted, and he said the writing was the whole of the spring. The ② draft, meaning the manuscript and not the plan, ran fourteen springs and stayed unnamed in the book; a draft, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unfinished.

Every ③ draft in that office had the same short margin at the side of it, and the ④ draft at the end, meaning the one they kept for the editor and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A draft, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to revise; my teacher said the revising is the part that fills fourteen springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the draft was the whole of the story, meaning the plan and not the manuscript. The ⑥ draft, meaning the plan and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody revises and nobody signs; draft, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a manuscript and a plan. He said the plan is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ draft had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short margin. The ⑧ draft of the whole thing, my teacher wrote in April, was one office and fourteen springs of revising; draft, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to revise. She said the revising was never mentioned.

The ⑨ draft I remember is the one named in the catalogue, which was signed in 1987 and is still described as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ draft, my mother said in 1989, is the only one that improves by being revised; every draft, she said, is a plan that has agreed to look like a manuscript. She said the plan was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 草稿；草案（指那间办公室里写就的那一稿）
B. n. 草稿；草案（指那一稿本身，与方案相对）
C. 固定搭配：write a draft 写一稿
D. n. 草稿；草案（指留给编辑的那一稿）
E. n. 草稿；草案（抽象总称，指一位作者的改稿之事）
F. n. 草稿；草案（指目录上写到、被列名的那一稿）
G. n. 草案；方案（指故事里人人都改却无人签字定稿的那样东西）
H. n. 方案（抽象总称，指人人都改却无人签字定稿的那种东西）

items.q: wrote a draft that no editor in the office would have accepted
The draft, meaning the manuscript and not the plan
the draft was the whole of the story
the draft had become a line in a catalogue
The draft of the whole thing
A draft, my mother said in 1989

answers.why: write a draft 意为“写一稿”，1966 年老师写了一稿，那间办公室里没有一位编辑肯接受它。
draft 意为“草稿、草案”，指那一稿本身而不是方案，它经过了十四个春天而在簿子上没有被记名。
draft 意为“草稿、草案”，指那间办公室里的每一稿，每一稿侧边都有同一道窄窄的页边。
draft 意为“草稿、草案”，指留给编辑的那一稿，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
draft 意为“草案、方案”，指故事里人人都改却无人签字定稿的那样东西，叔叔说这份方案就是那个故事的全部。
draft 意为“方案”，指人人都改却无人签字定稿的那种东西而不是那一稿，是故事里人人都改、却无人签字的东西。
draft 意为“草稿、草案”，指目录上写到、被列名的那一稿，到 1975 年这一稿成了目录里的一行。
draft 意为“草稿、草案”，老师四月写道，整件事的改稿之事是一间办公室和十四个春天的修改。
draft 意为“草稿、草案”，我记得的是目录上列名的那一稿，1987 年被签定了，至今仍被说成办公室里最安静的一稿。
draft 为抽象总称，母亲 1989 年说，一稿草稿是唯一会因为被好好修改而变得更好的东西。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1966 年老师写了一稿，那间办公室里没有一位编辑肯接受它，他说写着才是那个春天的全部。（write a draft）
那一稿，指的是那一稿本身而不是方案，经过了十四个春天而在簿子上没有被记名。（draft）
那间办公室里每一稿侧边都有同一道窄窄的页边。（draft）
末尾那一稿，指的是他们留给编辑的那一稿，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（draft）
叔叔说这份方案就是那个故事的全部，指的是方案而不是那一稿。（draft）
1989 年母亲说，一稿草稿是唯一会因为被好好修改而变得更好的东西。（draft）
answers: In 1966 my teacher wrote a draft that no editor in the office would have accepted, and he said the writing was the whole of the spring.

Every draft in that office had the same short margin at the side of it.
The draft at the end, meaning the one they kept for the editor and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the draft was the whole of the story, meaning the plan and not the manuscript.
